chapters.title: Teams, agents and routing
intro: This chapter is for supervisors and administrators. It covers the **Teams & Agents** module.
You use it to watch live workload, organise departments and teams, and decide who gets new tickets. You also manage agents, skills, shifts, leave and out-of-office delegates.

sections.title: The Teams & Agents module
intro: Open **Teams & Agents** in the left rail. Tabs across the top take you to each part of the module.

You see the module when your role includes `agents.manage` or `supervisor.monitor`. What you can change depends on your other permissions. The [permission reference](#permission-reference) lists every permission.

rows: Departments, their e-mail alias, routing team, business hours and SLA default.
Teams, their members, and how new tickets are routed to them.
Every agent with roles, departments, availability, load and last sign-in.
Invite and edit: `admin.users`. Routing profile: also `agents.manage`.
The skills catalogue used by skill-based routing.
Shift patterns, shift assignments, leave requests and the team calendar.
Shifts: `agents.manage` or `admin.organisation`. Anyone can request leave.
Anyone for themselves. `agents.manage` or `admin.users` for others.
The live monitor of agents, queues, SLA risk and waiting chats.

blocks.tip: Supervisors who cannot manage the organisation land on **Monitor** when they open the module. Everyone else lands on **Departments**.

sections.title: The live monitor
intro: The live monitor shows the current state of your departments on one screen. It refreshes by itself when tickets, chats or availability change. It also refreshes every minute.
You need `supervisor.monitor`. Supervisors see their own departments. Administrators see all departments.

blocks.caption: The live monitor filtered to the Customer Success department.
blocks.alt: Live monitor with numbered areas: live indicator, tabs, department filter, KPI tiles, agents table, queues, SLA risk list and chats waiting

callouts: **Live** shows that updates arrive as they happen. The refresh button reloads the view at once.
The module tabs.
The department filter. Choose **All my departments** or one department.
Tiles for agents online, open tickets, unassigned, SLA at risk, SLA breached and chats waiting.
**Agents**: availability, load against capacity, tickets in progress, overdue tickets, chats and idle time.
**Queues**: open, unassigned, at-risk and breached tickets for each team, with the oldest waiting ticket.
**SLA risk**: the riskiest open tickets, breached first, then by due time. Up to 50 are shown.
**Chats waiting**: visitors who wait for an agent, with the time they have waited.

list: **On leave** means the agent has approved leave now. **Off shift** means the agent is outside their shift. **Delegated** means a delegate covers the agent.
The load bar turns amber at 75% of capacity and red at 100%.
A waiting chat turns red after five minutes.

sections.title: Change an agent's availability from the monitor
sections.intro: Set an agent to **Online**, **Away**, **Busy** or **Offline** when they forgot to do it themselves.
prerequisites: Your role includes `agents.manage` or `admin.users`. Otherwise the availability shows as a badge only.
steps: In the **Agents** table, find the agent.
In the **Availability** list of that row, choose the new value.
sections.result: A message confirms the change, for example "Priya Raman is now Away". Routing uses the new availability at once.

sections.title: Reassign an at-risk ticket
sections.intro: Move a ticket that is about to breach, or has breached, to an agent with more room.
prerequisites: Your role includes `tickets.assign`. Otherwise the **Reassign** button is hidden.

steps.caption: The **Reassign** dialog for ticket #1010.
steps.alt: Reassign dialog with New owner and Note fields

steps: In **New owner**, choose an agent. The list shows the least loaded agents first.
Optionally, enter a **Note** for the new owner.
sections.result: A message confirms that the ticket is reassigned. The monitor refreshes.

blocks.note: The list offers agents of the ticket's department only. Agents on leave and the current owner are left out.

sections.title: Departments
intro: Every ticket belongs to exactly one department. The department's routing team, business calendar and SLA apply to its tickets.
Open **Teams & Agents** > **Departments** to see one card for each department.

blocks.caption: The **Departments** tab with one card for each department.
blocks.alt: Departments tab with numbered New department button, Show archived box, badges, details, edit and archive buttons and counts

callouts: **New department** creates a department.
**Show archived** adds archived departments to the list.
Badges show the department code, **In portal** and **Transfers need approval**.
The e-mail alias, routing team, business hours, default SLA and department head.
The edit button opens the department.
The archive button archives the department.
Links to the department's teams and agents, and its open tickets.

rows: 2–12 letters or digits. Left empty, the app makes one from the name.
A short explanation shown on the card.
Mail to this address lands in the department.
An agent shown as the head of the department.
The team that receives the department's new tickets. A new department gets a default team automatically.
The working hours for SLA clocks. **24x7** means no calendar.
Shown on the card. **Policy rules decide** leaves the choice to the SLA policies.
Customers can choose the department on portal forms.
Moving a ticket to another department creates an approval request first.
A number from 0 to 1000 that orders the departments in lists.

blocks.note: In this release, the department's **Default SLA policy** does not change which policy a ticket gets. Use SLA policy conditions instead. See [How a policy is chosen](#how-sla-policy-is-chosen).

sections.title: Create or edit a department
steps: Select **New department**, or select the edit button on a department card.

steps.text: Enter the **Name** and, if you want, a **Code** and **Description**.
steps.caption: The department dialog for Technical Support.
steps.alt: Edit department dialog with name, code, description, e-mail alias, head, routing team, calendar, SLA policy and options

steps: Enter the **E-mail alias** and choose the **Department head**.
Choose the **Routing team**, **Business calendar** and **Default SLA policy**.
Turn on **Visible in the customer portal** or **Transfers out need supervisor approval** if you need them.
sections.result: A message says "Department created" or "Department updated". The card shows the new details.

blocks.note: You can choose the **Routing team** only when you edit an existing department. A new department gets its routing team automatically.

sections.title: Archive or restore a department
sections.intro: Archive a department you no longer use. Archived departments receive no new tickets and disappear from the portal.
prerequisites: At least one other active department exists.

steps.text: Select the archive button on the department card.
steps.caption: The archive dialog asks where to move open tickets.
steps.alt: Archive Technical Support dialog with the Move open tickets to list

steps: If the department has open tickets, choose a department in **Move open tickets to**.
sections.result: A message says "Department archived". Open tickets move to the department you chose.

blocks.p: Moved tickets keep their owner when the owner belongs to the new department. Other tickets are routed again.

steps: Select **Restore** on the archived department's card.

blocks.note: You cannot archive a department that a brand uses as its default. Change the brand first.

sections.title: Teams and routing
intro: A team is a group of agents inside one department. Each department has one routing team that receives its new tickets.
Each team has routing settings. They decide which member gets a new ticket.

blocks.caption: The **Teams** tab filtered to the Technical Support department.
blocks.alt: Teams tab with numbered department filter, Test routing, New team, routing badges, routing, edit and delete buttons, and member list

callouts: The department filter.
**Test routing** opens a preview of who would get a sample ticket.
**New team** creates a team.
Badges show the assignment mode and routing options, such as **Shift-aware** and **Max 20 per agent**.
The routing button opens the team's routing settings.
The edit button opens the team.
The delete button. The department's routing team has no delete button.
Members with their availability and load. **Lead** marks the team lead.

rows: Nobody. Tickets wait in the team queue until someone picks or assigns them.
Eligible members take turns in a fixed rotation.
The eligible member with the lowest share of open tickets against capacity. This is the default.
The best match on product, category, territory, tier, language and skill levels, then load.
Members whose territory matches the customer's service region first, then load.

list: A customer's dedicated agent always gets the ticket first.
Routing skips inactive agents, light agents and agents who are not team members.
Routing skips agents on approved leave and agents with an active delegate.
Routing skips agents who are not online, when **Only agents who are Online** is on.
Routing skips agents who are off shift, when **Skip agents who are off shift** is on.
Routing skips agents who reached their own capacity or the team cap.

blocks.p: When nobody qualifies, the ticket goes to the **Fallback queue**. Without a fallback, it waits in the team queue.

blocks.note: **Skill based** routing uses each agent's average skill level. It does not yet match the skills a ticket needs.

sections.title: Create or edit a team
steps: Select **New team**, or select the edit button on a team card.

steps.text: For a new team, choose the **Department** and enter a **Name**.
steps.caption: The team dialog with its members and team lead.
steps.alt: Edit team dialog with department, name, description, members, team lead and Active option

steps: In **Members**, add the agents of the department.
Leave **Active (receives routed tickets)** on, unless the team should stop receiving tickets.
sections.result: A message says "Team created" or "Team updated".

blocks.note: You cannot move an existing team to another department. Light agents may be members, but they never own tickets.

sections.title: Set how a team routes tickets

steps.text: Select the routing button on the team card.
steps.caption: The routing dialog with the five assignment modes.
steps.alt: Routing dialog with assignment modes, online and shift options, team cap and fallback queue

steps: Turn on **Only agents who are Online** or **Skip agents who are off shift** if you need them.
In **Max open tickets per agent**, enter a team cap, or leave it empty.
In **Fallback queue**, choose the team that takes tickets when nobody here is eligible.
sections.result: A message says "Routing updated". New tickets for the team follow the new settings.

blocks.note: Routing settings apply to new tickets only. Manual assignment is never blocked.

sections.title: Delete a team
prerequisites: No open tickets wait in the team's queue.
steps: Select the delete button on the team card.
sections.result: A message says "Team removed".

blocks.note: A team with ticket history is deactivated instead of deleted. A department's routing team cannot be deleted. Choose another routing team first.

sections.title: Test routing for a sample ticket
sections.intro: See who would get a ticket right now, and why. Nothing is created or assigned.
steps: Choose the **Department**, and a **Team** if you want a team other than the routing team.
sections.result: The panel shows the agent who would get the ticket, or **Stays in queue**. A table lists every candidate with the reason for the result.

blocks.caption: **Test routing** shows Meera Iyer as the best match, with all candidates below.
blocks.alt: Test routing panel with the chosen agent and a table of candidates with availability, load, shift, result and score

blocks.p: **Fallback used** means nobody in the team qualified and the fallback team took the ticket. Select **Test routing** again to close the panel.

sections.title: The agents list
sections.intro: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Agents** to see every agent of your organisation.

blocks.caption: The **Agents** tab with plan seats, filters and the agents table.
blocks.alt: Agents tab with numbered Invite agent button, seats panel, search box, status, department and agent type filters, and table header

callouts: **Invite agent** sends an invitation. You need `admin.users`.
Seats used against your plan for agents and light agents, and pending invitations.
Search by name or e-mail.
Filter by status: **Active**, **Invited** or **Deactivated**.
Filter by department.
Filter by agent type: **Full agents** or **Light agents**.
Each row shows status, roles, departments, availability, load and last sign-in. Select a row to open the agent.

blocks.note: Full agents, administrators and pending invitations count against the agent seats. Light agents count against a separate limit.

sections.title: Invite an agent
sections.intro: Add a new person to your desk. They receive an e-mail with a code to choose their password.
prerequisites: Your plan has a free seat.

steps.caption: The **Invite an agent** dialog with sample details.
steps.alt: Invite an agent dialog with work e-mail, full name, title, time zone, light agent option, roles, departments, supervises and teams

steps: Enter the **Work e-mail** and **Full name**. Optionally, enter a **Title** and choose a **Time zone**.
Turn on **Light agent** if the person only views tickets and adds internal notes.
In **Roles**, choose one or more roles. Leave it empty to give the Agent role.
In **Departments**, choose at least one department.
sections.result: The **Invitation sent** dialog opens. It shows when the code expires and an accept link you can copy. Select **Done**.

blocks.note: The invitation code is valid for 72 hours. In demo mode, the dialog also shows the code itself.

sections.title: The agent page
sections.intro: Select an agent in the list to open their page. It shows who they are, what they can access and how routing treats them.

blocks.caption: The agent page for Priya Raman.
blocks.alt: Agent page with numbered Deactivate button, photo, status, availability, and Profile, Access, Routing profile, Shifts and Account-managed customers cards

callouts: Actions for the agent: **Deactivate**, **Reactivate**, **Resend invitation** or **Revoke**, depending on the status.
The photo. **Add photo**, **Change photo** and **Remove** appear for administrators and for the agents themselves.
Badges for status, **Light agent**, **MFA** and a pending or expired invitation.
**Availability**, with the time it last changed.
**Profile**: e-mail, phone, time zone, locale, last sign-in and e-mail signature.
**Access**: roles, departments (with supervisor marks), teams and the person the agent reports to.
**Routing profile**: capacity, languages, skills and routing attributes.
**Shifts**: the agent's shift assignments. **Manage shifts & leave** opens the **Shifts & leave** tab.
**Account-managed customers**: customers this agent manages. You set account managers on the customer record.

sections.title: Edit an agent's profile

steps.caption: The profile dialog with name, title, phone, time zone, locale and signature.

steps: Change the **Display name**, **First name**, **Last name**, **Title** or **Phone**.
Choose the **Time zone** and enter the **Locale**, such as `en` or `en-IN`.
Edit the **E-mail signature**. You can use basic formatting.
sections.result: A message says "Profile saved".

sections.title: Change an agent's roles and departments
prerequisites: You hold every permission of the roles you give or take away. See [The escalation guard](#escalation-guard).

steps.caption: The access dialog with roles, departments, supervised departments, teams and manager.

steps: In **Roles**, add or remove roles. Keep at least one role.
In **Departments**, add or remove departments. Keep at least one department.
sections.result: A message says "Access saved". The change applies to the agent's open sessions at once.

blocks.note: **Reports to** receives the agent's leave requests.
You cannot remove a department while the agent still owns open tickets in it. Reassign those tickets first.

sections.title: Edit an agent's routing profile
sections.intro: The routing profile tells routing how much work the agent can take and what they are good at.

steps.caption: The routing profile with capacity, languages, skills and a territory attribute.
steps.alt: Routing profile dialog for Priya Raman

steps: Enter **Max open tickets** and **Max concurrent chats**.
In **Languages**, add language codes such as `en`, `hi` or `ta`.
Under **Skills**, select **Add skill**, choose a skill and its level from 1 (basic) to 5 (expert).
Under **Routing attributes**, select **Add attribute**, choose the kind and enter or choose the value.
sections.result: A message says "Routing profile saved". The card shows the new capacity, skills and attributes.

rows: 1–1000. Default 25. Routing stops at this number.
0–50. Default 3. Live chats the agent can hold at once.
Skills from the catalogue, each with a level from 1 to 5.
**Territory**, **Product**, **Customer**, **Language**, **Category** or **CustomerTier**. Territory and skill-based routing use them.

sections.title: Set an agent's availability
prerequisites: You are the agent, or your role includes `admin.users` or `agents.manage`.
sections.result: A message says "Availability set to" and the new value.

sections.title: Change or remove an agent's photo
prerequisites: You are the agent, or your role includes `admin.users`.
steps: Choose a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image of up to 2 MB.
sections.result: A message says "Photo updated". To take the photo away, select **Remove** under it.

sections.title: Resend or revoke an invitation
sections.intro: Use these actions while an agent has the status **Invited**.
steps: Select **Resend invitation** to send a new code. The **Invitation sent** dialog opens.
Or select **Revoke**, then **Revoke** again in the confirmation.
sections.result: A resent invitation has a new 72-hour code. A revoked invitation frees the seat, and the person cannot join.

sections.title: Deactivate an agent
sections.intro: Deactivate an agent who leaves. They are signed out everywhere, cannot sign in, and their seat is freed.
prerequisites: The agent is not the last active administrator.

steps.caption: The deactivate dialog asks what happens to the agent's open tickets.
steps.alt: Deactivate Priya Raman dialog with Route again, Give to an agent and Return to the team queue options

steps: Under **Their open tickets**, choose **Route again**, **Give to an agent** or **Return to the team queue**.
If you chose **Give to an agent**, choose the **New owner**.
sections.result: A message confirms the deactivation and how many open tickets are being reassigned. The status changes to **Deactivated**.

blocks.warning: The agent loses access at once. Check the open tickets choice before you select **Deactivate**.

blocks.p: **Give to an agent** moves only the tickets of departments that the new owner belongs to. Other tickets go back to the queue.

sections.title: Reactivate an agent
prerequisites: Your plan has a free seat.
steps: In the agents list, choose **Deactivated** in the status filter.
sections.result: A message says the agent is reactivated. They can sign in again.

sections.title: Manage the skills catalogue
sections.intro: Skills are things such as products, modules or languages. You give agents a level for each skill in their routing profile.

steps.caption: The **Skills** tab with the skills catalogue.
steps.alt: Skills tab with numbered New skill button, filter box, table and edit and delete buttons

steps.text: Select **New skill**, or the edit button on a skill row.
steps.caption: The **New skill** dialog with a name and category.
steps.alt: New skill dialog with Name, Category and Description

steps: Enter the **Name**, and optionally a **Category** and **Description**.
sections.result: A message says "Skill added" or "Skill updated". The **Agents** column shows how many agents have the skill.

blocks.p: To delete a skill, select its delete button and confirm. Agents who have the skill lose it.

blocks.tip: Type in **Filter skills** to find a skill in a long list.

sections.title: Shifts
intro: A shift is a weekly working pattern in a time zone. You assign agents to a shift from a start date.
Shifts matter only for teams with **Skip agents who are off shift** turned on. Agents without a shift count as always on shift.

blocks.caption: The **Shifts & leave** tab with three shift patterns.
blocks.alt: Shifts and leave tab with numbered Request leave and New shift buttons, inner tabs and a shift card

callouts: **Request leave** and **New shift**.
Inner tabs: **Shifts**, **Assignments**, **Leave** and **Calendar**. **Leave** shows how many requests wait.
A shift card: colour, weekly hours, time zone, hours per week and agents on it today.
The edit and delete buttons.

sections.title: Create or edit a shift

steps.text: Select **New shift**, or the edit button on a shift card.
steps.caption: The shift dialog with weekly hours from Monday to Friday.
steps.alt: Edit India day shift dialog with name, time zone, colour, description, weekly hours and Active

steps: Enter the **Name**, choose the **Time zone** and pick a **Colour**.
Under **Weekly hours**, select a preset, such as **Mon–Fri 09–18**.
Adjust each day. Tick a day to make it a working day, and enter the start and end times.
To add a break, select **Split** and enter a second interval. A day can have up to four intervals.
sections.result: A message says "Shift created" or "Shift updated".

blocks.tip: **Copy Monday to weekdays** copies Monday's hours to Tuesday to Friday. The end time can be `24:00`.

blocks.p: To delete a shift, select its delete button and confirm. Its assignments are removed too.

sections.title: Assign agents to a shift

steps.text: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Shifts & leave**, then the **Assignments** tab.
steps.caption: The **Assignments** tab lists each agent's shift and whether they are on shift now.
steps.alt: Assignments tab with the Assign shift button and a table of agents, shifts, dates and status

steps.caption: The **Assign shift** dialog.
steps.alt: Assign shift dialog with Shift, Agents, From and To

steps: Choose the **Shift** and one or more **Agents**.
Enter the **From** date. Optionally, enter a **To** date.
sections.result: A message says "Shift assigned" with the number of agents.

blocks.p: An empty **To** date means open-ended. A new assignment closes any older assignment that overlaps it.
To remove an assignment, select the remove button on its row and confirm.

sections.title: Leave
intro: Agents request leave on the **Leave** tab. Approved leave takes the agent out of routing for the period. Their existing tickets stay with them.
A request goes to the person the agent reports to. If nobody is set, it goes to a supervisor of one of the agent's departments. If there is none, anyone with `approvals.decide` can decide it.

blocks.caption: The **Leave** tab with one request waiting for approval.
blocks.alt: Leave tab with numbered status filter, Request leave button and Approve and Reject buttons

callouts: The status filter: **All**, **Awaiting approval**, **Approved**, **Rejected** or **Cancelled**.
**Request leave**.
**Approve** and **Reject** appear when you may decide. **Cancel** appears on leave you may cancel.

rows: The agent is skipped by routing during the period.
Declined. The reason shows in the **Reason** column.
Withdrawn before or during the period.

sections.title: Request leave

steps.caption: The **Leave** dialog with a reason filled in.
steps.alt: Leave dialog with Agent, Starts, Ends, Type and Reason

sections.result: A message says "Leave requested" and "Sent for approval". The request appears on the **Leave** tab as **Requested**.

blocks.note: A request cannot overlap another leave request of the same agent.

sections.title: Record leave for an agent
sections.intro: Managers can enter leave for someone else, for example a sick day reported by phone.
steps: Enter the dates, the **Type** and a **Reason**.
sections.result: A message says "Leave recorded". Leave you record for someone else is approved at once.

sections.title: Approve or reject leave
prerequisites: The request waits for you. Or your role includes `approvals.decide` and also `agents.manage` or `admin.users`.
The leave is not your own.
steps: Open **Teams & Agents** > **Shifts & leave**, then the **Leave** tab.
Choose **Awaiting approval** in the status filter.

steps.caption: The approval dialog with an optional note.
steps.alt: Approve leave dialog for Arjun Nair with a Note field

steps: Optionally, enter a **Note**. The agent sees it.
sections.result: A message says "Leave approved" or "Leave rejected". The calendar updates.

sections.title: Cancel leave
prerequisites: The leave is your own, or your role includes `agents.manage` or `admin.users`.
The leave is requested or approved, and has not ended yet.
sections.result: The status changes to **Cancelled**, and routing includes the agent again.

sections.title: The team calendar
sections.intro: The **Calendar** tab shows leave, leave requests, delegations and the holidays of the default business calendar. Use it to spot gaps before you approve leave.

blocks.caption: The **Calendar** tab for November 2026 with a holiday.
blocks.alt: Month calendar with a legend for leave, requested leave, delegations and holidays

blocks.p: Select **Month** or **Week** to change the view. Use the arrows to move between periods, and **Today** to come back.

sections.title: Set up a delegation
sections.intro: A delegation names someone to cover for an agent who is away. While it is active, routing skips the away agent. Their new assignments and approval requests go to the delegate.
prerequisites: To set up a delegation for someone else, your role includes `agents.manage` or `admin.users`.

steps.caption: The **New delegation** dialog with a delegate and reason.
steps.alt: New delegation dialog with Away, Delegate, From, To, Reason and two options

steps: In **Away**, keep **Me** or choose the agent who will be away.
In **Delegate**, choose the agent who covers.
Enter the **From** and **To** dates and times, and a **Reason**.
Leave **Route approval requests to the delegate** on, unless approvals should wait.
Turn on **Also move open tickets when the window starts** to hand over open tickets too.
sections.result: A message says "Delegation created". The delegation shows as **Scheduled**, then **Active** when the period starts.

blocks.note: Delegations of one agent cannot overlap. The delegate cannot be away during the same period.

sections.title: Edit or end a delegation
steps: To change dates or options, select the edit button on the row, change the values, then select **Save**.
To stop a delegation early, select **End now**, then **End now** again in the confirmation.
sections.result: An ended delegation shows the state **Ended**. Turn on **Show ended** to see past delegations.

troubleshooting.problem: Your plan allows a number of agents and they are in use.
troubleshooting.cause: Every agent seat of the plan is taken. Pending invitations also use a seat.
troubleshooting.fix: Deactivate an agent or revoke an unused invitation. Or upgrade the plan.

troubleshooting.problem: Your plan allows a number of light agents and they are in use.
troubleshooting.cause: The light-agent limit of the plan is reached.
troubleshooting.fix: Deactivate a light agent, or upgrade the plan.

troubleshooting.problem: "The department has 21 open tickets. Choose a department to move them to."
troubleshooting.cause: You archive a department that still has open tickets.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose a department in **Move open tickets to**, then select **Archive**.

troubleshooting.problem: "A brand/portal uses this department as its default."
troubleshooting.cause: A brand sends its portal tickets to this department.
troubleshooting.fix: Change the brand's default department first, then archive.

troubleshooting.problem: "10 open tickets are queued in this team. Move them before deleting the team."
troubleshooting.cause: The team still has tickets in its queue.
troubleshooting.fix: Assign or move the queued tickets, then delete the team.

troubleshooting.problem: "This is a department's default routing team."
troubleshooting.cause: You try to delete a department's routing team.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose another **Routing team** on the department first.

troubleshooting.cause: You opened your own agent page.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask another administrator to deactivate your account.

troubleshooting.cause: The agent already has leave in that period.
troubleshooting.fix: Change the dates, or cancel the other request first.

troubleshooting.problem: "Another delegation for this agent overlaps the period."
troubleshooting.cause: Two delegations of one agent cannot cover the same time.
troubleshooting.fix: End or edit the other delegation, or pick other dates.

troubleshooting.problem: An agent never gets new tickets.
troubleshooting.cause: The agent is offline, off shift, on leave, delegated, at capacity, a light agent, or not a team member.
troubleshooting.fix: Use **Test routing** on the **Teams** tab. The **Result** column gives the reason for each agent.

faq.q: Does approved leave move an agent's tickets?
faq.a: No. Approved leave only stops new tickets from reaching the agent. To hand over open tickets, reassign them. Or set up a delegation with **Also move open tickets when the window starts**.

faq.q: Why does an agent without a shift still get tickets at night?
faq.a: Agents without a shift count as always on shift. Shifts also matter only for teams with **Skip agents who are off shift** turned on.

faq.q: Can a light agent be a team member?
faq.a: Yes. Light agents can be members and see the team's tickets. Routing never gives them tickets, and they cannot own tickets.

faq.q: Does Test routing assign the sample ticket?
faq.a: No. **Test routing** only shows who would get the ticket and why. Nothing is created or assigned.

glossary.definition: The rule a team uses to pick the agent for a new ticket: Manual, Round robin, Load balanced, Skill based or Territory.
The most open tickets an agent may own, set in the routing profile. Routing stops giving tickets to an agent at capacity.
An out-of-office arrangement. While it is active, the away agent's new assignments and approval requests go to a delegate.
The team that receives a team's new tickets when none of its own members can take them.
A collaborator who can view tickets and add internal notes, but never replies to customers or owns tickets.
An agent's capacity, chat limit, languages, skills and routing attributes, which routing uses to pick an agent.
The team that receives a department's new tickets.
A weekly working pattern in a time zone. Teams can skip agents who are outside their shift.
A product, module, language or other ability that agents hold at a level from 1 to 5.
